discovery: Discovery of superconductivity in organic molecular conductors

nominees.name: Denis Jérome
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique des Solides, CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and unconventional superconductivity
motivation: In 1980 Bechgaard designed and synthesized the (TMTSF)2X charge-transfer salts, and Jérome, applying high pressure, discovered superconductivity in (TMTSF)2PF6: the first superconductor made of organic molecules. This joint achievement of chemistry and physics created a new class of materials whose soft lattices and narrow bands can be tuned continuously by pressure, strain, chemical substitution or controlled disorder. The Bechgaard salts and their successors, the κ-(BEDT-TTF)2X family, became clean model systems for fundamental problems of correlated electrons: the proximity of superconductivity to spin-density-wave and Mott insulating states, the bandwidth-controlled Mott transition and its critical endpoint, quasi-one-dimensional non-Fermi-liquid physics, and quantum spin liquids. Forty-five years of worldwide research grew from this discovery, which anticipated the central theme of unconventional superconductivity near magnetic order found later in cuprates and iron pnictides.
